items.description: You can now minimize downtime when you copy data across containers in Azure Cosmos DB accounts. You can use online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB to copy data from one container to another in real time. Your application using the source container remains online while the data is being copied to the destination container in real time. After your data is completely copied, you can switch over to the new container.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Announcing a new mTLS enhancement in Azure Application Gateway for backend applications that perform client certificate and authorization header validation at the backend while still requiring web traffic inspection through the Web Application Firewall (WAF). This update introduces greater flexibility by allowing such applications to accept and inspect traffic through the Application Gateway even when a client certificate is not presented, supporting mixed authentication scenarios with both mTLS and token-based access.What ChangedPreviously, Application Gateway listeners operated in Strict mode, blocking any connection without a valid client certificate. This meant traffic relying solely on authorization tokens could not reach the backend.With this update, you can now enable Passthrough mode for mutual TLS (mTLS) connections, allowing:Requests without client certificates to pass through WAF for inspection.Backend applications to retain full control over certificate and token validation logic.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Application Gateway mTLS passthrough support

items.description: Announcing the preview of JSON Web Token (JWT) validation in Azure Application Gateway — enabling authentication and token validation right at the Application gateway before traffic reaches your backend applications or APIs.Why It mattersProtect at the perimeter: Block requests with missing or invalid tokens (401/403) at the edge, ensuring only trusted traffic reaches your services.Boost performance: Offload token validation from your microservices or web apps to improve scalability and response times.Simplify operations: Apply consistent authentication policies centrally across multiple applications and routes.What’s included in the previewIssuer (iss) validationAudience (aud) matching - supports Client ID and/or custom App ID URIsExpiration (exp) enforcementSignature verification using JWKSLearn more.
items.title: Public Preview: JWT Validation in Azure Application Gateway

items.description: Custom error pages are now generally available on App Service. When using custom error pages you can configure your apps to present an error page of your choosing instead of the default error pages that are presented to your users. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Custom error pages on Azure App Service

items.description: Announcing the retirement of Windows Server 2022 on Azure Kubernetes Service enabled by Azure Arc in October 2026.
items.title: Retirement: Windows Server 2022 on Azure Kubernetes Service enabled by Azure Arc

Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.
items.title: Retirement: Migrate to dedicated VM for your compute clusters

items.description: We’re bringing Azure Monitor’s dynamic threshold capabilities to Log search alerts!Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.Key benefitsDynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:Learn the historical behavior of log query results.Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts

items.description: Azure Database for MySQL triggers for Azure Functions are now generally available, enabling you to set up change tracking and develop event-driven applications at scale on any MySQL table. You can trigger a function when a row in a MySQL table is created, updated, or deleted.    Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL Triggers for Azure Functions

items.description: Now you can deploy Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in all three availability zones in Japan West.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server availability zones expansion in Japan West

items.description:
On October 1, 2026 extended
support for Python 3.10 will end. Your
apps that are hosted on App Service will continue to run, but security updates will
no longer be available, and we’ll no longer provide customer service for Python 3.10. Learn more about App Service language support. Required
action To avoid
potential security vulnerabilities and minimize risk for your App Service apps, follow the steps to upgrade your app to Python 3.11 before October 1, 2026.
items.title: Retirement: Support for Python 3.10 ends on October 1st, 2026

items.description:
Azure Functions now supports custom
handlers in Flex consumption. Custom handlers are lightweight web servers that
receive events from the Functions host. Any language that supports HTTP
primitives can implement a custom handler.  Custom handlers are best suited for
situations where you want to: Implement
a function app in a language that's not currently offered out-of-the box, such
as Go or Rust. Implement
a function app in a runtime that's not currently featured by default, such as
Deno.  With custom handlers, you can use triggers and input and output
bindings via extension bundles. Learn more:Get
started with Azure Functions custom handlers with quickstarts
in Go and Rust.Review the documentation.
items.title: Generally Available: Custom handler support in Azure Functions Flex consumption

items.description:
Azure
Container Apps support for premium ingress is now generally available. This
feature introduces environment-level ingress configuration options, with the
primary highlight being customizable ingress scaling. This capability supports
the scaling of the ingress proxy, enabling customers to better handle higher
demand workloads, such as large performance tests. By configuring your ingress
proxy to run on workload profiles, you can scale out more ingress instances to
handle more load. Running the ingress proxy on a workload profile will incur
associated costs.  To further
enhance the flexibility of your application, this release includes other
ingress-related settings, such as termination grace period, idle request
timeout, and header count. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Premium Ingress in Azure Container Apps

items.description:
Azure Container Apps support for rule-based routing is now
generally available. This feature provides greater flexibility and
composability to your Azure Container Apps by simplifying your architecture for
microservice applications, A/B testing, blue-green deployments, and more.  Rule-based routing allows you to direct incoming HTTP
traffic to different apps within your Container Apps environment based on the
requested host name or path. This includes support for custom domains. Instead
of having to configure a separate reverse proxy, such as NGINX, you can now
provide routing rules for your environment and incoming traffic will
automatically be routed to the specified target apps. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Rule-based routing in Azure Container Apps

items.description:
Azure
Container Apps now supports deployment labels in public preview as a new
deployment mode. This feature simplifies environment management and enables
advanced deployment strategies for your applications by allowing you to assign
meaningful names—such as dev, staging, or prod—to specific container revisions. Deployment
labels provide a flexible way to manage traffic routing and revision control
without renaming revisions or manually adjusting configurations. These include: Streamline environment management by grouping revisions under
descriptive labels. Route traffic intelligently based on labels for A/B testing,
staged rollouts, and blue-green deployments. Promote or roll back revisions quickly using label history,
ensuring smooth transitions and minimal downtime. With
deployment labels, you gain greater control over your application lifecycle
while reducing complexity in multi-environment scenarios.   Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Deployment labels in Azure Container Apps

items.description:
Azure Container Apps now supports dynamic shell sessions in public
preview. A shell session is a platform-managed built-in container used to
run and execute common shell commands in an isolated sandboxed
environment.  With Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions supporting empty shell
sessions and an integrated MCP server, customers can instantly provide agents
with secure, isolated sandboxes for tasks like code execution, tool testing, or
workflow automation. This enables seamless integration into agent frameworks,
allowing agents to access disposable compute environments on demand. Customers benefit from rapid provisioning, enhanced security, and reduced operational
overhead for agentic workloads. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic sessions shell environment and MCP support in Azure Container Apps

items.description:
Announcing the general availability of JavaScript (JS) challenge for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) with Azure
Front Door To strengthen bot mitigation strategies,
Azure WAF now introduces JS challenge as a new security feature. The
JS challenge provides an invisible, frictionless layer of protection by
distinguishing legitimate users from malicious bots without requiring human
interaction. Unlike CAPTCHA, this challenge runs silently in the background,
reducing user disruption while effectively blocking harmful automated traffic. Key benefits include: Enhanced
bot protection: Malicious bots fail
the JS challenge, safeguarding your applications. Improved
user experience: Legitimate users
are not interrupted, ensuring seamless access. Flexible
integration: Available as a mitigation action in the Bot
Managed ruleset and custom rules. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure WAF JavaScript challenge on Azure Front Door

items.description: Azure Monitor now offers one-click enablement of recommended alerts directly in the Azure Portal for Azure Monitor Managed service for Prometheus customers. These alerts enable you to monitor the ingestion limits for Azure Monitor Workspace and avoid metrics throttling.Learn more
items.title: Public Preview: Recommended alerts for Azure Monitor Workspace

items.description: The Object REST API, an S3-compatible REST API, on Azure NetApp Files bridges the gap between traditional file-based storage and modern cloud services, enabling customers to use their existing data in new ways. By providing integration via Microsoft Fabric with Azure AI services, native S3 access from modern applications, and other Azure services, customers can unlock new use cases, reduce costs, and accelerate innovation. Learn more:  What's new in Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn Understand Azure NetApp Files object REST API access | Microsoft Learn Configure object REST API access in Azure NetApp Files | Microsoft Learn
items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files Object REST API

items.description: Breakthrough mode in Azure NetApp Files enables extreme performance and scalability for demanding HPC and EDA workloads. It supports large volumes up to 2PiB, delivering throughput up to 50GiBps, depending on workload characteristics. Breakthrough mode uses six storage endpoints for each large volume ensuring consistent performance. Storage systems hosting breakthrough mode volumes are reserved for each customer to provide peak performance and not compete with other workloads. Key benefits include: High-capacity scaling for large-scale, latency-sensitive workloads Simplified network management with multiple storage endpoints per volume Dedicated capacity stamps to eliminate noisy neighbor interference and maintain predictable performance Supported in all regions where large volumes are supported. How to create a volume with large volume breakthrough mode enabled.  Create an NFS volume Create an SMB volume Create a dual protocol volumeLearn more.
items.title: Public preview: Support for large volume breakthrough mode

items.description:
Azure Monitor metric
alerts now support all Azure metrics - including platform,
Prometheus, and custom metrics - giving you complete coverage for your monitoring
needs. In addition, metric alerts now offer powerful query capabilities with PromQL, the industry-standard query language, on Prometheus
metrics, OTel-based VM performance counters, and other OTel
custom metrics ingested into Azure Monitor Workspace (AMW). Key Capabilities:
 PromQL-based
     conditions: Leverage the full power of PromQL for sophisticated metric
     selection, aggregation, and transformation. 
 Flexible
     scoping: Choose between resource-centric alerts for
     granular RBAC or workspace-centric alerts for
     cross-resource visibility. 
 Managed
     Identity support: Securely authorize queries using Azure Managed
     Identity. 
 Customizable
     notifications: Add dynamic custom properties and custom email subjects
     for faster triage and context-rich alerting. With query-based metric alerts, you can detect
complex patterns, reduce alert noise, and reuse
existing community-based Prometheus alert logic - all while
maintaining a unified monitoring experience in Azure. This feature empowers
teams to proactively manage performance and reliability at scale, without
sacrificing flexibility or security.
items.title: Public Preview: Query-based metric alerts in Azure Monitor

items.description: Blob storage Object Replication metrics for pending operations and pending bytes are now generally available in all regions. These replication metrics will empower you to optimize the performance, troubleshoot replication delays, and maintain high availability across your Object Replication policies. The two metrics that will provide deeper visibility and insights into your object replication progress are: Pending Operations: Tracks the total number of operations pending replication from the source to the destination storage account of your OR policy Pending Bytes: Tracks the total volume of data pending replication from the source to the destination storage account of your OR policy Both metrics are emitted in time buckets (e.g. <5min, 5-10 min, 10-15 min, etc.) which show how long your operations have been pending replication to the destination account.  This assists with quickly identifying delays in the replication pipeline and makes it easier to monitor replication performance.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Object Replication Metrics

items.description: Azure Backup has introduced threat detection capabilities for Azure VM backups, powered by Microsoft Defender for Cloud (MDC). This new capability enables customers to assess the health of their Azure VM backup restore points (RPs) by identifying malicious or ransomware-infected backups.By leveraging signals from Microsoft Defender for Servers, Azure Backup detects indicators of compromise such as disruption patterns, heuristic behavior anomalies, and malware or ransomware signatures. This feature is now in public preview in limited regions.
items.title: Public Preview: Threat Detection in Azure Backup powered by MDC

items.description: Now you can use the open-source DocumentDB Kubernetes Operator to run DocumentDB on Kubernetes. DocumentDB is a Mongo-DB–compatible, open-source document database built on PostgreSQL. The operator extends Kubernetes with custom resource definitions (CRDs) and makes it easier for you to deploy and manage DocumentDB clusters using familiar tools such as kubectl and Helm. Learn more.
items.title: Open Source: Announcing the DocumentDB Kubernetes Operator

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE for geospatial queries, now generally available. With this feature, you can sort query results by their distance from a given point or GeoJSON object directly within Azure Cosmos DB. You no longer need to calculate distances in application code or perform client-side sorting. This function makes it easier to deliver real-time, location-aware experiences for logistics, retail, mapping, and smart-city scenarios with less code and better performance, such as “find the nearest store,” “list drivers by proximity,” or “rank properties by distance.” By handling sorting within the database engine, queries become simpler, faster, and more efficient, reducing latency and round-trip overhead. ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE works seamlessly with existing spatial data types and indexing in Azure Cosmos DB, providing consistent performance and accuracy at global scale. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL Geospatial Queries

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL includes Query Advisor, now generally available in the .NET SDK. Query Advisor helps you write faster, more efficient queries by analyzing your query structure and providing clear, actionable recommendations. It identifies ways that can potentially reduce Request Unit (RU) cost and improve performance. As your applications grow, even small changes in query design can have a big impact on scalability and cost. Query Advisor reviews your queries, detects patterns that may cause excessive scans or processing, and suggests improvements, such as optimized filters, more efficient array operations, or simplified subqueries. Each recommendation includes a brief explanation and an example rewrite so you can learn and decide what to apply.  This feature helps developers and database engineers understand how to fine-tune queries for their workloads, achieve better performance, and control RU consumption. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Query Advisor in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Announcing the general availability of a dedicated Azure Standard Load Balancer in Azure Database for MySQL - Flexible Server for high availability-enabled servers. With this feature, a high availability configuration gets the benefit of a dedicated Standard Load Balancer, including low latency, high throughput network traffic distribution of front-end requests to backend servers. With Standard Load Balancer managing the MySQL data traffic path, you can enjoy a more optimized failover time for high availability servers. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL – Flexible Server now supports high availability with dedicated Azure Standard Load Balancer

items.description: You can now configure read replicas (in-region and geo-replicas) with Premium SSD v2 storage tier in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Read replicas enable you to scale out read-heavy workloads and improve performance by offloading read operations to replica servers, while write operations continue on the primary. In addition, geo-replicas can serve as read-write failover servers in the event of a disaster, enhancing your business continuity strategy.  Replication is performed asynchronously using the native physical replication technology in PostgreSQL, enabling you to replicate from a primary server to up to five replicas.  With Premium SSD v2, each managed disk delivers up to 80,000 IOPS. When combined with five read replicas, you can achieve up to 480,000 IOPS, helping you meet the demands of your most performance-intensive workloads. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL read replicas with Premium SSD v2

items.description: In early November 2025, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL:  Azure SQL Hyperscale now supports multiple geo-secondary replicas, making it easier to design and deploy disaster recovery topology spanning multiple regions. Learn more. Azure SQL Database enables you to restart your database in the Azure portal.  The portal uses the same API that is available for PowerShell, REST, and Azure CLI.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for early November 2025

items.description: GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) is now available in public preview. GitHub Copilot in SSMS helps you write Transact-SQL (T-SQL) faster and with greater accuracy. Using database and connection context, it can also answer general SQL questions and assist with administrator tasks, directly in your SSMS environment. GitHub Copilot in SSMS can answer questions for databases in SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and SQL databases in Microsoft Fabric. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: GitHub Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)

items.description:
Azure Copilot introduces specialized
agents (gated preview) to help migrate,
operate, and modernize workloads anywhere. Copilot evolves chat into an
immersive, full-screen command center (public preview) powered by GPT-5
reasoning, artifact generation, and ARM-driven scenarios. Customers get
contextual, multi-modal, and personalized experiences, including chat history
and inline actions. A compliance-first architecture and Bring Your Own Storage
(public preview) let customers manage chat data securely and control data
residency. The new agents (gated preview) are as follows:
 Deployment
     Agent:
     Streamlines environment planning and guided infrastructure deployment.
 Migration
     Agent:
     Automates cloud migration, generates AI recommendations, and modernizes
     apps.
 Optimization

     Finds cost and carbon savings and enables direct action.
 Observability
     Agent:
     Diagnoses full-stack app issues and suggests mitigation using Azure
     Monitor.
 Resiliency
     Agent:
     Offers resiliency insights, auto-remediation, and ransomware protection.
 Troubleshooting
     Agent:
     Pinpoints issues, suggests fixes, and guides AKS troubleshooting.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot brings new intelligent agents to support end-to-end lifecycle management of workloads

items.description: Azure Monitor now offers a unified, single-click onboarding experience for both Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters and virtual machines (VMs). This new experience simplifies setup by automatically deploying the latest Azure Monitor capabilities with optimized defaults.For AKS, the experience combines managed Prometheus metrics, container logs with Kubernetes events, and our newly GAed Dashboards with Grafana. As a part of the new experience, we are also introducing a new application monitoring addon and preconfigured AKS recommended alerts for faster troubleshooting.For VMs, the onboarding includes new OpenTelemetry-based metrics (now in public preview and free), legacy Log Analytics counters, and recommended VM alerts for comprehensive performance visibility.This unified experience provides a consistent, streamlined approach to monitoring across your compute environments, helping you get started with Azure Monitor in minutes.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor unified onboarding experience for AKS and VMs

items.description:
Geo priority replication enhances the replication process
for GRS and GZRS storage accounts by enabling accelerated data replication
between the primary and secondary regions. This feature is backed by a Service
Level Agreement (SLA), ensuring the Last Sync Time for Block Blob data remains
at 15 minutes or less, 99.0% of the billing month. With this guaranteed sync
time, users can feel more confident about their data’s durability and
availability, especially if an unexpected outage occurs in their primary region
and a failover is required. Geo Priority Replication applies to Block Blob.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Geo Priority Replication for Azure Blob

items.description:
Object replication priority replication will allow users to
obtain prioritized replication from the source to the destination storage
account of their replication policy. When you enable priority replication, you
can benefit from the associated Service Level Agreement if your source and
destination account are located within the same continent. The SLA will
guarantee 99.0% of operations are replicated from the source container to the
destination container of your OR policy within 15 minutes for the billing month.Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Object Replication Priority Replication for Azure Blob

items.description: With Azure NetApp Files single file restore from backup, you can restore individual files from Azure NetApp Files backup vault without needing to restore an entire volume. By restoring only the necessary files, you can save time and cost needed for restoring data. This feature is available in all ANF supported region. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure NetApp Files single file restore from backup

items.description:
Planned Failover is a customer-managed failover that
provides the ability to failover your geo-redundant storage account while
keeping geo-redundancy and data durability. You can seamlessly swap the
primary and secondary storage endpoints of your geo-redundant
account. After the Planned Failover is completed, all new
write operations will be directed to the original secondary region,
which will serve as the new primary region. Planned Failover can be
utilized in a variety of scenarios including disaster recovery drills,
partial outages where storage remains healthy or proactive disaster
preparation. It is now generally available for GPv2 storage accounts and
is compatible with Blob, ADLS Gen2, Table, File, and Queue data.  Learn
more.
items.title: Generally Available: Planned Failover for Azure Storage

items.description: Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available in the Retail feed. This release includes updates to Azure Sphere OS only; it does not include an updated SDK. If your devices are connected to the internet, they will receive the updated OS from the cloud.This release includes quality and underlying build system updates.For self-help inquiries or technical support, review the Azure Sphere support options.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available

items.description: In November 2025, the following updates and enhancements were made to Azure SQL: View, modify, insert rows in a table without manually writing T-SQL code using the interactive Edit Data interface in the MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. Learn more. Import and export DACPACs—now available in the MSSQL extension. Apply DACPAC files to new or existing databases or generate new files from existing databases. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for November 2025

Learn more.  Optimize performance and costs by adding extra memory to Azure SQL Managed Instance. Learn more. New improvements in optimized locking further reduce the overhead of locks in the SQL database engine. Learn more.Boost your SQL queries with powerful Regex support for advanced pattern matching. Learn more. Bigint support in DATEADD for extended range calculations. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for November 2025

items.description: Microsoft Foundry introduces new ready-to-use, customizable AI templates for popular use cases such as live voice agents, release management, data unification, and SharePoint integration applications. These templates eliminate repetitive setup tasks, reduce deployment friction, and accelerate the journey from concept to production. With customizable code samples, pre-integrated Azure services and GitHub-hosted quick-start guides, development teams can launch faster, customize easily, and scale securely on Microsoft’s trusted AI infrastructure. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: New AI templates in Microsoft Foundry

items.description: SQL Server 2025, the AI-ready enterprise database, is now generally available, marking a major milestone in Microsoft’s mission to modernize enterprise data platforms. This release introduces built-in AI capabilities, seamless integration with Microsoft Fabric and Azure, and enhanced developer productivity through familiar T-SQL extensions. Now you can boost performance and security using intelligent query processing, optimized concurrency, and Microsoft Entra-based identity management.  SQL Server 2025 is designed for hybrid environments—on-premises, multi-cloud, and edge—delivering enterprise-grade reliability and compliance while enabling next-generation AI scenarios. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Availabe: SQL Server 2025

items.description: A new SQL Server migration in Azure Arc solution streamlines and accelerates your journey to Azure SQL Managed Instance. Powered by Azure Database Migration Service and assisted by Copilot, it delivers an automated, end-to-end migration process that includes continuous assessments, simplified provisioning, and real-time replication. The capabilities in SQL Server migration in Azure Arc include:Continuous assessment reporting that automatically delivers readiness, cost, and technical insights. Streamlined provisioning. You can select or provision Azure SQL targets directly within the portal, eliminating context switching. Real-time data replication via distributed availability groups (DAGs). Instead of a complex, multiple-step setup, you get a simplified replication process without the need to navigate separate portals. Read-only replica validation. You can test target instances before cutover, avoiding rework. Client connection summaries that continuously identify which clients connect to each SQL instance, replacing manual tracing. Copilot assistance and troubleshooting that guides you through the migration steps, reducing manual effort and delays. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: New SQL Server migration in Azure Arc

items.description: Announcing that the mssql-python driver is now generally available. This milestone marks a major step forward in delivering a modern, high-performance, and developer-friendly experience for Python developers working with SQL Server, Azure SQL Database, and SQL databases in Microsoft Fabric. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Microsoft Python driver for SQL Server

items.description: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) has long been the trusted tool for managing SQL databases, writing T-SQL, and troubleshooting issues. With SSMS 22, built on Visual Studio 2026, you get support for SQL Server 2025, improved integration with SQL databases in Fabric, and native compatibility on Windows ARM64 devices. This release also introduces the GitHub Copilot preview, giving you AI-powered assistance for T-SQL authoring and optimization directly within SSMS. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) 22

items.description: The labels() function in KQL graph semantics is now generally available. This function enables you to retrieve, filter, and project label information for nodes and edges in your graph queries, making it easier to work with categorized graph data.The labels() function works with graph models in both Fabric Eventhouse and Azure Data Explorer, allowing you to:Filter graph elements by their labels to focus on specific node or edge typesProject label information in query results for better data understandingUse labels with collection functions like any(), all(), and map() for advanced pattern matchingAccess labels of intermediate nodes in variable-length paths using inner_nodes()Labels can be either static (fixed labels assigned to node or edge types) or dynamic (labels derived from data properties during graph construction), giving you flexibility in how you organize and query your graph data.Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: labels() function in KQL graph semantics

items.description: Announcing openCypher support for KQL graph semantics, bringing the widely adopted open-source graph query language to your graph data. This update allows you to run openCypher queries on any Fabric Eventhouse or Azure Data Explorer, making it easier to work with graph data using a popular, declarative pattern matching syntax.openCypher provides ASCII-art style pattern matching that intuitively represents graph relationships, making complex graph queries more readable and easier to write.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: openCypher support for KQL graph semantics

items.description:
LocalDNS for AKS is
now generally available.   Large-scale Kubernetes clusters often face DNS resolution
delays and reliability issues, especially during upstream outages or high query
volumes. To address this, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now offers LocalDNS, a
feature that is generally available. LocalDNS deploys a DNS proxy on each node, enabling faster
and more reliable DNS resolution by handling queries locally. This eliminates
bottlenecks, reduces latency, and ensures continued resolution even during
upstream DNS outages through configurable serve-stale settings. With no application-level changes required, LocalDNS
delivers immediate performance improvements and supports advanced DNS
customization for both internal and external domains. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: LocalDNS for AKS

items.description:
Diagnosing and resolving issues in Kubernetes clusters can
be complex and time-consuming, especially when navigating logs, telemetry, and
diagnostics manually. To simplify this experience, Azure Kubernetes Service is
introducing a new agentic AI-powered CLI experience through the “az aks agent” command. This new capability brings agentic reasoning directly into
the Azure CLI, allowing developers and operators to interact with their
clusters using natural language. By describing an issue or query, users can
trigger an intelligent agentic loop that gathers signals from multiple sources,
analyzes diagnostics, identifies health issues and root causes, and provides
actionable recommendations. The CLI agent also integrates with the AKS MCP
server and can seamlessly create and manage an Azure OpenAI instance, though it
supports any LLM provider. Powered by HolmesGPT - an open-source project co-maintained by the AKS team and accepted as a CNCF sandbox project- this feature is now available in public preview. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Agentic CLI for AKS

items.description:
Maintaining consistent and secure node configurations in
Kubernetes environments can be challenging due to issues like configuration
drift, manual changes, and complex upgrade paths. These challenges often lead
to unpredictable behavior and increased operational overhead. Azure Kubernetes Service now supports Flatcar Container
Linux in public preview. Flatcar is built on an immutable filesystem, which
helps ensure predictable node behavior by preventing unauthorized changes and
simplifying recovery from security incidents. As a Cloud Native Compute
Foundation (CNCF) project, Flatcar also supports cross-cloud deployment, making
it a strong choice for organizations seeking enhanced security and operational
efficiency across diverse environments. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Flatcar Container Linux for AKS

items.description:
Container network metrics
filtering in Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS) is now available in
public preview. In
containerized environments, the ingestion of excessive network metrics can lead
to inflated storage costs and cluttered dashboards, making it difficult to
maintain observability efficiency. Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS)
now offers container network metrics filtering, available in public preview, to
address this challenge. This new
capability enables users to define fine-grained filters at the Cilium level
using a Custom Resource Definition (CRD), allowing metrics collection to be
scoped by namespace or pod. By filtering metrics before they reach Prometheus,
organizations can significantly reduce data volume, lower operational overhead,
and improve the clarity of their observability tools.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Container network metrics filtering in Advanced Container Networking Services for (ACNS) for AKS

items.description:
Local redirect policy with Azure
CNI powered by Cilium for AKS is now generally available. Customers running high-scale AKS workloads often experience
latency and performance bottlenecks due to cross-node traffic routing. The new local
redirect policy addresses this by enabling node-local service routing, ensuring
traffic is redirected to pods on the same node whenever possible. This results
in lower latency, improved throughput, and enhanced reliability, especially
critical for AI training and microservice-based applications.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Local redirect policy in Azure CNI powered by Cilium for AKS

items.description:
Pod CIDR expansion in Azure CNI
Overlay for AKS is now available in public preview. To meet the growing demands of dynamic and large-scale
Kubernetes workloads, Azure Kubernetes Service now offers Pod CIDR Expansion in
public preview for clusters using Azure CNI Overlay. While Azure CNI Overlay
already delivers scalable pod IP address management via a logical overlay
network, many enterprise customers require additional flexibility to support
evolving business needs. This new capability allows users to expand existing pod CIDR
ranges, enhancing both scalability and adaptability for workloads that require
more IP space. The preview currently supports CIDR range expansion only,
enabling organizations to better manage IP allocation without redeploying
clusters. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Pod CIDR expansion in Azure CNI Overlay for AKS

items.description: You can now configure immutability for Azure SQL Database LTR backups to meet compliance and regulatory needs. Once immutability is configured, the backups can’t be edited or deleted until the specified retention expires, mitigating any potential ransomware attacks for the entire retention.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Database long-term retention (LTR) backup immutability

items.description:
eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS is now available in public preview. As containerized applications scale across distributed environments,
traditional networking approaches can introduce latency and reduce throughput.
To address this, Azure CNI powered by Cilium now offers eBPF Host Routing in
public preview for Azure Kubernetes Service. This feature uses eBPF technology to embed routing logic
directly into the Linux kernel, eliminating the need for iptables and reducing
reliance on the host network stack. By enabling Cilium to make direct routing
decisions, eBPF host routing delivers lower latency, fewer network hops, and
higher throughput for Kubernetes clusters. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS

items.description: The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now integrates GitHub Copilot, bringing AI-powered SQL assistance directly into your development workflow. Together, they help you reduce repetitive tasks, accelerate development, and design database schemas and applications faster and more intelligently. With just a few clicks in Visual Studio Code, you can generate T-SQL and object-relational mapping (ORM) code, explore schemas, and build, analyze, and optimize queries—even if you’re new to SQL.  This general availability release brings a more complete GitHub Copilot experience, including Ask mode, Agent mode, and slash commands. You can use natural language and interact in multiple ways with your SQL Server, Azure SQL, or SQL database in Microsoft Fabric. You also get more detailed connection information, clearer error messages, better database context awareness, and improved guidance—enhancements that make GitHub Copilot easier and more natural to use as part of your daily workflow.  Whether you’re building modern web apps, cloud-native solutions, or AI-driven experiences, GitHub Copilot helps you understand the business logic within your database, follow best practices for security and performance, and even generate mock data for rapid testing.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: MSSQL extension integration with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code

items.description: Announcing the public preview of vector indexing using DiskANN in Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance and SQL database in Microsoft Fabric. DiskANN is an algorithm for efficient vector similarity search, making it ideal for product recommendations or image search applications. Designed for large-scale vector search and recommendation systems, DiskANN seamlessly integrates with the existing capabilities of Microsoft SQL query engine, enabling you to build complex, multimodal semantic search capabilities in modern applications.  This release follows the general availability of the vector data type and vector functions announced this summer, giving you foundational AI capabilities right in the database engine. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL Database DiskANN vector indexing

items.description:
To address the growing need for granular traffic control in
microservices architectures, Azure Container Networking Services now offers
Layer 7 Policy as a generally available feature. This capability empowers
customers to enforce fine-grained traffic controls at the application layer,
supporting protocols such as HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, and Kafka. By bridging gaps in
zero-trust enforcement and microservice isolation, Layer 7 Policy enhances
security posture, provides deeper traffic visibility, and simplifies policy
management, all without compromising performance. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Layer 7 policy with Advanced Container Networking Services (ACNS) for AKS

items.description:
Cluster-wide Cilium network
policy for AKS clusters using Azure CNI powered by Cilium is now Generally
Available.   Managing consistent network policies across Kubernetes
namespaces has long been a challenge for platform teams, especially in
multi-tenant environments. With the general availability of cluster-wide Cilium
network policy for AKS clusters using Azure CNI powered by Cilium, customers
can now define and enforce network policies at the cluster level. This
enhancement simplifies policy management and strengthens isolation between
tenants by leveraging Cilium’s high-performance eBPF dataplane. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Cluster-wide Cilium network policy with Azure CNI powered by Cilium for AKS

items.description: The Next‑gen General Purpose tier delivers a major performance boost while preserving the cost advantages you expect. You get more power and compute flexibility without sacrificing the simplicity of a fully managed platform as a service (PaaS) experience.  You can immediately get 3 to 5 times better performance simply by upgrading from the classic General Purpose tier. For more demanding workloads, you can fine‑tune your environment using configurable IOPS and adjustable memory‑to‑vCore ratios, getting the control you need to optimize without adding unnecessary costs.  With Next‑gen General Purpose, you can run heavier workloads, scale with confidence, and achieve a better price-to-performance balance—all while staying on a fully managed service. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance Next-gen General Purpose service tier

items.description:
Organizations running complex workloads on Kubernetes often face
challenges in optimizing pod placement for performance, cost, or resource
efficiency. To address this, Azure Kubernetes Service now offers scheduler
profile configuration with in-tree plugins, available in public preview. This
new capability enables users to customize scheduling behavior and define
workload priorities across specific nodes or the entire cluster. It’s
especially beneficial for advanced scenarios such as data processing, AI/ML, and
cost-optimized workload distribution. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Scheduler profile configuration for AKS

items.description:
MCP support for AI toolchain operator add-on is
now Generally Available.    The AI Toolchain Operator add-on now supports
KAITO inference workspaces with integrated tool calling and Model Context
Protocol (MCP), addressing key challenges around dynamic model interaction and
real-time data integration.   Previously, developers faced friction deploying
LLM-based services that needed external tool access, such as APIs or custom
functions, often requiring bespoke orchestration. Now, you can benefit from
seamless integration of KAITO’s vLLM-based tool calling with supported models,
along with MCP support for connecting models to external systems in real time –
to enable smarter, more context-aware AI services directly within AKS. Learn more:about Integrate tool calling with LLM Inference with the AI toolchain operator add-on on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)about Integrate an MCP server with an LLM Inference Service on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
items.title: Generally Available: MCP support for AI toolchain operator add-on in AKS

items.description: Announcing that Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server now supports the Azure Storage extension with Parquet format and multiple compression options. You can seamlessly read and write Parquet files directly from your database, enabling faster data exchange with analytics and storage systems while reducing storage costs through efficient compression. With this capability, you can simplify your data pipelines, improve performance for large-scale workloads, and optimize your cloud storage usage—all without leaving your PostgreSQL environment. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL storage extension support for Parquet

items.description:
Cloud-native workloads face increasingly sophisticated
threats—from rootkits and container escapes to unauthorized code execution—that
demand stronger security guarantees. To address these challenges, Microsoft has
introduced Azure Linux with OS Guard, now available in public preview. Built on the FedRAMP-certified Azure Linux 3.0 base, OS
Guard is a next-generation immutable container host that enforces immutability,
code integrity, and mandatory access control. It leverages advanced
technologies like dm-verity, SELinux, and Integrity Policy Enforcement
(IPE)—recently upstreamed in Linux kernel 6.12—to ensure only trusted binaries
from signed sources can run, while locking down user space against tampering.
With Trusted Launch enabled by default, OS Guard also secures boot components
using measured integrity backed by vTPM keys. Azure Linux is the trusted OS powering Microsoft’s own
fleet, and OS Guard builds on that foundation to deliver enhanced protection
for cloud-native environments. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Linux OS Guard for AKS

items.description: You can now bring data together and simplify analytics using Microsoft Fabric mirroring for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, now generally available. Mirroring in Fabric unifies your organizational data in OneLake and supports network-isolated servers (using virtual networks or private endpoints) and highly available configurations. To enhance app integration with rich business insights, you can join data across various sources and enjoy one-click integration with Microsoft Power BI. For swift, efficient access, you can optimize your data using the Delta Lake table features. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Mirroring in Fabric for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

items.description: Announcing that the PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code is generally available. With this powerful tool, you can connect to PostgreSQL database instances, run queries, create and manage connection profiles, and take advantage of Microsoft Entra ID support, context-aware IntelliSense, syntax highlighting, and SQL formatting. Designed to boost your productivity and streamline development, the extension includes automated local database container deployments in Docker and the ability to chat with GitHub Copilot. With this extension, you can manage your PostgreSQL databases directly within your development environment, eliminating the need for context switching.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code with GitHub Copilot

items.description: You can now use PostgreSQL 18 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL. This release introduces the latest PostgreSQL innovations along with seamless in-place upgrade support, allowing you to move from earlier versions without changing your server endpoint, reconfiguring applications, or migrating data manually. You can stay current with minimal downtime and reduced operational complexity while benefiting from a fully managed service.  PostgreSQL 18 delivers significant improvements in performance, scalability, and developer productivity, including asynchronous I/O (AIO) for faster queries, enhanced vacuuming, UUIDv7 support, logical replication enhancements, and virtual generated columns for flexible schema design. By adopting PostgreSQL 18 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL, you gain access to the newest community features with enterprise-grade reliability, built-in security, and high availability. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: PostgreSQL 18 with in-place upgrade on Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: You can now stream data changes in near real time from Azure SQL Database directly into Azure Event Hubs. With the public preview of change event streaming (CES), you can streamline data integration and support enhanced analytics, event-driven architectures, and the modernization of monolithic applications.  By streaming operational data from SQL databases to Azure Event Hubs, you can seamlessly integrate this data into real-time dashboards, microservices, and various downstream systems, reducing the delays and complexities associated with traditional batch-based pipelines. Data is transferred from SQL only once and can be accessed by multiple consumers, minimizing polling on operational databases. Additionally, when data is available on a common message bus, it becomes more accessible for new consumers, unlocking faster innovation such as AI solution development.  CES offers near real-time latency, an “at least once” message delivery guarantee, and minimal impact on source workloads.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure SQL change event streaming

items.description: Now you can create pg_duckdb extensions in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, so you can accelerate analytics using DuckDB’s vectorized, columnar execution.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server pg_duckdb extension

items.description: Now you can deploy general purpose and memory-optimized v6-series Azure Virtual Machines with local NVMe storage in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. The v6 series is available with either Intel or AMD processor options. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server v6 series VMs and AMD v6 Confidential Compute

items.description: The anon extension is now generally available in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. This extension provides data anonymization tools. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server anon extension

items.description: Announcing the public preview of Microsoft Foundry support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. The Azure PostgreSQL MCP Server is now natively integrated with Microsoft Foundry.  This integration enables you to build AI agents to securely query and analyze PostgreSQL data using natural language, with support for data retrieval, vector search, schema discovery, and more.  With enterprise-grade security via Microsoft Entra ID, plus support for row-level access controls, this release accelerates AI adoption across your organization.  You can onboard in minutes using the Microsoft Foundry SDK or the Microsoft Agent Framework to build agents that interact with the Azure Database for PostgreSQL MCP Server. For added data security, you can also self-host the MCP Server using Azure Container Apps or Azure Functions on their own Azure subscriptions and virtual networks. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Native Microsoft Foundry support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: Now you can use elastic clusters to horizontally scale Azure Database for PostgreSQL through row-based and schema-based sharding. Elastic clusters make it easy to build multitenant apps by offloading shard management and operations—such as tenant isolation, split, or online rebalancing of shards—to the service.   Row-based sharding is ideal for multitenant software as a service (SaaS) deployments, as it splits tenants into rows within a cluster-distributed table, enhancing density and improving margins per tenant. Alternatively, schema-based sharding suits microservices and lift-and-shift migrations of existing applications, offering more customization of schemas for each tenant.  Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Elastic clusters on Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server

items.description: Announcing the general availability of the 2025 REST API for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. This release adds support for PostgreSQL 17 and 18, so you can adopt new versions without changing your automation patterns. You can also now set the default database name for elastic clusters. To improve the developer experience, we have renamed operation IDs for clearer navigation, and corrected HTTP response codes so scripts and retries behave as expected. Security guidance gets a boost with a new customer-managed key (CMK) encryption example that demonstrates automatic key version updates. Finally, the specification is easier to use with renamed files for accuracy, a reorganized structure that simplifies browsing and diffs, and enhanced local definition metadata—delivering a clearer, safer, and more capable API for your 2025 roadmaps. Learn more
items.title: Generally Available: 2025 REST API for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

items.description: Migrating from Oracle to PostgreSQL is now simpler and faster with the new Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration tooling, available directly in the Azure Database for PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code.  This new tool helps you seamlessly convert your Oracle schemas and application code to PostgreSQL equivalents without leaving your development environment. You can extract Oracle schema files, validate conversions in a scratch PostgreSQL database, and review AI-assisted conversion recommendations—all through a step-by-step guided wizard inside Visual Studio Code.  The tool automatically identifies Oracle-specific constructs and transforms them into PostgreSQL-compatible syntax while flagging any items that require developer review. In the background, integration with Azure OpenAI Service brings intelligent code conversion to both database and application layers, reducing manual rework and accelerating migration readiness.  In addition to database schema conversion, the new Application Migration capability leverages GitHub Copilot Agent Mode together with specialized Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversion tools to modernize client application code.  Whether you’re modernizing a single application or moving enterprise workloads, this tool helps you streamline end-to-end migration, ensure compatibility, and get to PostgreSQL faster. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Oracle to PostgreSQL migration tooling in Visual Studio Code

items.description:
Microsoft
Azure now offers built-in Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmarks in
public preview for all Azure endorsed Linux distributions through Azure Machine
Configuration’s new customizable security benchmarks capability, powered by azure-osconfig’s compliance engine. This capability allows organizations
to easily customize and apply industry-standard security benchmarks which are
in parity with the content published on CIS website. It supports both Level
1(L1) and Level 2(L2) server profiles, enables exception and parameter
customization, operates in audit-only mode at no additional cost, and extends
compliance management to hybrid scenarios via Azure Arc. Using this new capability,
you can introduce a flexible, compliance as code driven approach to your
organization to maintain security and compliance across your hybrid
infrastructure. The solution is officially certified by CIS for CIS
benchmark assessment for all the supported benchmarks.  Learn more:Read our blog and
refer to the documentation.  For any questions or feedback fill out this
short form.
items.title: Public Preview: Built-in CIS benchmarks for Azure endorsed Linux distros in Machine Config

items.description:
Announcing Managed Instance on Azure App Service, now in Public Preview! This new capability makes it easy to move web apps to the cloud with minimal configuration—no code rewrites required. Whether your .NET apps run on-premises or in VMs, you can move to a fully managed PaaS environment, future-proof your infrastructure, and unlock cloud benefits.Why Managed Instance?Many organizations still
rely on older .NET apps for critical tasks like billing, HR, compliance, and
reporting. These apps often depend on Windows-specific features and custom
tools, which makes rewriting them expensive and risky. With Managed Instance on Azure App Service,
they can keep operating with critical dependencies on local Windows services,
third-party vendor libraries, and custom runtimes without requiring any code
changes. The result is faster app modernization with lower overhead, and access to
cloud-native scalability, built-in security and Azure’s AI capabilities.Key Benefits:Full App Service experience with turnkey scaling, resiliency, and integrated services.Greater control via RDP access through Bastion, custom configurations, and identity management.Compatibility for complex workloads, including classic .NET Framework apps, without code changes.As part of a holistic migration and modernization strategy, Managed Instance simplifies app modernization, reduces costs, and accelerates your journey to the cloud.
items.title: Public Preview: Managed Instance on Azure App Service

items.description: Announcing the general availability of seamless, self-serve online migrations from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU to Azure DocumentDB—directly from the Azure portal. With this release, your organization can modernize its MongoDB workloads with zero downtime, no cost, and minimal operational overhead.  The migration engine reads natively from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU and writes to Azure DocumentDB, ensuring compatibility and performance across diverse workloads. It supports both offline and online migrations. Microsoft Entra ID integration and partition-level read optimization are already available.  You can start using this capability today to accelerate the journey to Azure DocumentDB—unlocking advanced features, improved performance, and a future-ready architecture. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Online migration from Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU to Azure DocumentDB

items.description: You can now migrate MongoDB workloads to Azure DocumentDB using the new Azure DocumentDB Migration extension for Visual Studio Code—now available in public preview. This seamless, zero-cost migration supports both online and offline modes, simplifying and accelerating your modernization journey.  The migration jobs run entirely on Azure–managed resources, maintained by the Azure Cosmos DB team, so you don’t need to install or manage any infrastructure. You can initiate and monitor migrations without staying connected throughout the process, making it ideal for secure and large-scale scenarios. The extension also supports private endpoint-enabled targets, ensuring enterprise-grade security and compliance.  Whether you're migrating from self-hosted MongoDB, MongoDB Atlas, or other compatible sources, this extension provides a unified, intuitive experience directly within Visual Studio Code. You benefit from improved performance, reduced operational overhead, and a streamlined path to Azure DocumentDB—all without incurring additional migration costs. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Online and offline migrations in Azure DocumentDB Migration extension

items.description: You can now help protect sensitive data from unauthorized access using dynamic data masking (DDM), a server-side, policy-based security feature in Azure Cosmos DB. DDM dynamically masks data for non-privileged users, ensuring that sensitive information is redacted in real time before being presented to applications, while the original data remains unchanged in the database.  DDM can help your organization meet security, compliance, and regulatory requirements by limiting exposure of sensitive data, including personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information (PHI). Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Dynamic data masking with Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Microsoft is announcing the general availability of Azure DocumentDB, a fully managed document database service built on the open-source, MongoDB-compatible DocumentDB, now governed by the Linux Foundation. Formerly known as Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore), Azure DocumentDB gives you the power of open source with the performance, security, and scale of Azure.   What you gain: Freedom and flexibility. Build once and deploy anywhere with a consistent open-source MongoDB-compatible database that runs across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. AI-ready innovation. Use built-in vector and hybrid search to power retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), copilots, and other intelligent applications. Elastic performance. Get instant autoscale and independent compute and storage scaling—so you pay only for what you use. Enterprise-grade reliability and security. Protect your data with Microsoft Entra ID authentication, customer-managed keys, and 35-day backups at no additional cost, backed by 99.999% uptime full-stack service-level agreements and around-the-clock Azure support.  With Azure DocumentDB, you can modernize your MongoDB workloads, build AI-driven apps faster, and scale globally on an open, flexible, and enterprise-ready foundation. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB - an open-source, MongoDB-compatible document database service for hybrid and multicloud

items.description: Now you can more easily operate your Azure Cosmos DB accounts at scale. Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools give you new capabilities when building multitenant software as a service (SaaS) applications.  You can simplify capacity management by creating a pool of throughput (RU/s) that can be shared by accounts in the fleet. You get all the security and performance isolation benefits of creating one Azure Cosmos DB account to represent a tenant or end customer, while also efficiently sharing RU/s resources across tenants to avoid overprovisioning at the per-tenant level. Throughput pooling is now generally available. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools

items.description: You can now unify insights across your entire Azure Cosmos DB footprint using Azure Cosmos DB Fleet Analytics, available in public preview. Fleet Analytics helps you manage data across multiple accounts, subscriptions, and workloads, providing large-scale, cross-account analytics for Azure Cosmos DB.   You can analyze performance, usage, and billing trends in one place, so you can manage growth, optimize efficiency, and ensure consistency across your fleet. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB Fleet Analytics

items.description: You can now enable priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB to ensure that high-priority requests are favored during periods of contention. The system will throttle low-priority requests first, allowing high-priority operations to proceed on a best-effort basis.  Using the Azure Cosmos DB SDK, you can assign each request a priority level (high or low). Low priority requests are retried according to the configured retry policy, helping maintain responsiveness for critical workloads. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: Integrated into the DocumentDB for VS Code extension, the Index Advisor enables you to view and debug database performance. It uses natural language to recommend optimal indexing and best practices for your MongoDB workloads.  Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Index Advisor for Azure DocumentDB

items.description: Now generally available, Cosmos DB in Fabric enables you to build operational and analytical workloads in Microsoft Fabric. You can use the AI-features in Azure Cosmos DB plus the innovations in Fabric to run SQL queries over JSON data and build real-time intelligence over transactional data. You can also use Azure Cosmos DB as a lightning fast serving layer for Microsoft Power BI, using Spark for reverse extract, transform, load (ETL)—all without having to stitch together separate services.   Cosmos DB in Fabric includes many new features, such as user-defined functions for seamlessly connecting to your Cosmos DB artifacts. With support for continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), you can manage development, test, and production pipelines. This release also supports Cosmos DB autoscaling for elasticity when you need it, and vector and full-text indexing and search are enabled by default to support your AI-enabled workloads. We are also announcing Fabric CMK support in Preview. This release marks a major step toward making operational data readily accessible across the Fabric ecosystem. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Cosmos DB in Microsoft Fabric

items.description: Now generally available, Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Fabric enables you to seamlessly integrate your existing operational workloads with the analytical capabilities of Microsoft Fabric. You can take advantage of the innovations in Fabric, running SQL queries over JSON data and building real-time intelligence over your existing transactional data. You can integrate your data with the Microsoft Fabric ecosystem of services and work with Copilot-assisted Microsoft Power BI—all without having to stitch together separate services.   With Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Fabric, you can select the containers to mirror into Fabric, giving you complete control over the data used for analytics. You get the best of both worlds—the latency and availability of Azure Cosmos DB and the array of analytical capabilities in Microsoft Fabric. This release makes it even easier to make your existing operational data accessible across the Fabric ecosystem. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric

items.description: Developers today are building more intelligent, connected, and autonomous applications than ever before. From personalized chatbots and copilots to dynamic content engines and decision systems, data is the foundation of these agentic experiences.  Azure Cosmos DB already plays a central role in powering these workloads, offering globally distributed, low-latency, highly scalable data services with flexible API support. However, developers told us they wanted a way to interact with their Cosmos DB data directly from Visual Studio Code (VS Code), where they already spend most of their time writing, debugging, and testing code.  With this release, we’re delivering exactly that—a unified, fast, and developer-first experience for working with Azure Cosmos DB data without leaving your coding environment.  Now generally available, Azure Cosmos DB for VS Code comes with significant updates focused on usability, stability, and performance. It incorporates months of feedback from preview users, who helped shape this extension into the powerful tool it is today. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB for Visual Studio Code

items.description: We are thrilled to announce the General Availability of a highly requested feature: Self-serve configuration of the lower_case_table_names server parameter during server creation. For MySQL version 8.0+ you can configure lower_case_table_names only when you're initializing the server. For restore operations or replica server creation, the parameter will automatically be copied from the source server and cannot be changed.   Learn more
items.title: General Availability: Server Parameters support for lower_case_table_names in Azure Database for MySQL- Flexible Server

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB now supports float 16 data types for vector indexes. With this update, you can store and query vectors using half-precision floating-point numbers. Using float16 cuts storage usage in half compared to float32, while maintaining high retrieval accuracy for most AI workloads.  Float16 can be especially useful for large-scale scenarios when you need to store many vector embeddings. By reducing vector size, you can lower indexing and storage costs, making it easier to scale semantic search and AI agent memory retrieval. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Float16 data type for vector indexes in Azure Cosmos DB

items.description: This release gives you faster vector inserts and index builds in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, helping you reduce end-to-end ingestion and indexing times for large AI workloads. This improvement is powered by algorithmic enhancements to our vector indexing engine. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Vector indexing performance improvements in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports fuzzy search in full-text search. With fuzzy search, you can deliver typo-tolerant, error-resilient search experiences directly within Azure Cosmos DB, helping your users find the right results even when queries or the data itself contain errors. This feature improves the quality and usability of search-driven applications, making them feel more natural and forgiving for end users. Learn more.
items.title: Generally Available: Fuzzy search in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL full-text search

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now offers an MCP Toolkit that can be used with Microsoft Foundry  Agent Service, available today in public preview.  This new integration allows you to connect Microsoft Foundry Agents directly to data in Azure Cosmos DB. By deploying the Azure Cosmos DB MCP Toolkit Server in your Azure environment, you can enable your agents to perform secure data operations and run semantic searches within Azure Cosmos DB.  The toolkit includes multiple ready-to-use tools that simplify setup and configuration, helping your agents discover data and retrieve the right information for reasoning and task execution. You can now build data-aware agents that respond to user requests with information drawn from live operational data. The integration in Microsoft Foundry  Agents Service makes it easy to connect to the MCP server and get started.  With vector search, full-text search, and high-performance NoSQL capabilities built into Azure Cosmos DB, your AI solutions can deliver faster and more contextually relevant results at a global scale.Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Azure Cosmos DB MCP ToolKit for Microsoft Foundry Agent Service

items.description: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports Italian and Portuguese languages in full-text search, available today in public preview. This update adds to the list of supported languages, enabling you to build rich, language-aware search experiences that understand the linguistic nuances of Italian and Portuguese text.  You can more easily create multilingual applications that deliver a natural and localized search experience for users across Europe and Latin America. Whether you’re building e-commerce catalogs, customer knowledge bases, or AI-powered chat and discovery tools, you can now seamlessly search across Italian and Portuguese content without needing to preprocess or translate data. Learn more.
items.title: Public Preview: Support for Italian and Portuguese in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL full-text search

items.description: Azure NetApp Files cache volumes are now available in public preview. The cache volumes feature is a new capability built on NetApp’s ONTAP FlexCache technology that provides a persistent, high-performance cache in Azure for data stored on ONTAP-based storage volumes outside of Azure NetApp Files. This feature enables organizations to cache active (“hot”) data closer to users and cloud applications, dramatically improving data access speeds and throughput over WAN connections. With cache volumes, you can burst on-premises datasets to Azure with near-local performance, which is ideal for scenarios such as running computational workloads in Azure or enabling globally distributed teams to collaborate without file transfer delays.    Cache volumes is available in these regions.  Learn more:   What's new in Azure NetApp Files Configure a cache volume for Azure NetApp Files
items.title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files cache volumes

items.description:
Azure Backup vaulted protection
for ADLS Gen2 delivers secure, off‑site backups to help organizations meet
resilience and compliance goals. Vaulted backups maintain an independent copy
of your data, isolated from the source account - providing protection against
accidental deletion, malicious activity, and ransomware.  Capabilities at a Glance: Off‑site protection: Recover data safely
by restoring to alternate storage accounts to support clean recovery
workflows. Automated & flexible scheduling: Configure
daily or weekly backup policies and trigger on‑demand backups when
needed. Long‑term retention: Store backups for up
to 10 years to meet compliance and archival requirements. Security‑first design: Soft‑delete,
immutability, encryption, and multi‑user authorization protect backup data in
the vault. Scope and availability at GA: Vaulted backups can be configured for block blobs in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 accounts. General availability will start with a subset of the regions from Public Preview list. We will continue expanding to additional regions over the coming
months. Learn more:Configure

available,

groups, identifying and associating virtual networks with the right IPAM pools
can become increasingly complex. Unassociated virtual networks may consume
overlapping address spaces, raising the risk of conflicts during provisioning. With Pool

virtual networks within their Network Manager scope that are not yet
associated with an IPAM pool. The feature intelligently recommends the
most suitable pool for each virtual network by applying longest-prefix
matching within the pool hierarchy, ensuring optimal fit and capacity
alignment. Administrators can bulk
select and associate virtual networks in a single action directly from the
Azure portal—streamlining operations, reducing manual effort, and ensuring full
coverage at scale. This
general availability release empowers customers to manage address spaces more
efficiently, minimize configuration drift, and maintain consistent governance
across large, distributed Azure environments. Learn more.

introduces a built-in validation mechanism to proactively detect and prevent
such conflicts. With

cycle. Key Capabilities

 Simplified

     tier transitions inside smart tier, early deletion or data retrieval fees.

balance and securely process non-HTTP(S) traffic for applications that rely on

proxy and establishes a new connection to the backend servers. The TLS
certificate management is available for both HTTPS and TLS protocols on a
resource, simplifying the certificate operations and providing a single
endpoint for clients. With this
release, the TLS/TCP proxy also brings support for Client
IP preservation using the PROXY protocol header, as well as support for
port 22 on listeners. This capability
is available on Application Gateway Standard v2 and WAF v2 SKUs. Learn
more.
